# Simplyblock Documentation

> Simplyblock is a cloud-native, software-defined storage platform that provides NVMe-over-TCP block storage for Kubernetes and Linux, with erasure coding, snapshots, clones, and multi-tenancy.

Every page of this documentation is available as Markdown: append `.md` to any page URL, or request the page with an `Accept: text/markdown` header. The complete documentation as a single file: https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/llms-full.txt

## Overview

- [Home](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/index.md): Home: Welcome to the Simplyblock Documentation, the comprehensive resource for understanding, deploying, and managing simplyblock's cloud-native platform.
- [Upgrades](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/upgrades/index.md): Upgrade simplyblock.
- [K8s Upgrade With Maintenance Window Upgrade (R25 to R26)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/upgrades/upgrade-notes-r25-r26.md): Maintenance-window procedure to upgrade a Kubernetes cluster from the R25 Helm charts to the R26 Simplyblock Operator, from node shutdown to workload restart.

## Important Notes

- [Important Notes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/index.md): Important Notes: Simplyblock is a high-performance distributed block storage optimized for Kubernetes that is compatible with any Linux.
- [Terminology](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/terminology.md): Terminology: A simplyblock storage cluster is a group of interconnected storage nodes that work together to provide a scalable, fault-tolerant, and.
- [Acronyms & Abbreviations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/acronyms.md): Reference table of Simplyblock acronyms and abbreviations used across architecture, deployment, operations, Kubernetes, NVMe, and security documentation.
- [Documentation Conventions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/documentation-conventions.md): Documentation Conventions: Features in simplyblock are released when reaching general availability.
- [Contributing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/contributing.md): Contributing: Simplyblock's documentation is publicly available, and contributions from the community to improve clarity, fix errors, and enhance it are welcome.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/index.md): The architecture of simplyblock: one NVMe-oF storage platform for block, shared file (pNFS), and object storage, with its components and core concepts.
- [What is Simplyblock?](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/what-is-simplyblock.md): Simplyblock is a distributed, NVMe-native storage platform for Kubernetes, which serves block, shared file, and object storage with predictable low latency.
- [Simplyblock Architecture](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/simplyblock-architecture.md): The simplyblock architecture: Simplyblock Operator, control plane, CSI driver, and a distributed storage plane with separate front storage and back storage.
- [Performance and QoS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/storage-performance-and-qos.md): How simplyblock keeps storage latency low and predictable, from its user-space NVMe data path to data placement, and how caps and service classes isolate I/O.
- [High Availability and Fault Tolerance](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/high-availability-fault-tolerance.md): How simplyblock keeps volumes available through device, node, rack, and site failures: erasure coding, failover paths, the write journal, and replication.
- [Deployment Topologies](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/deployment-topologies/index.md): How simplyblock places its control plane, operator, and storage nodes: local or hub-based management combined with HCI, disaggregated, or hybrid storage.
- [Deployment Topologies / Control Plane and Operator](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/deployment-topologies/control-plane-and-operator.md): Placement of the simplyblock control plane and Simplyblock Operator: local on every Kubernetes cluster, or centralized on a hub cluster with lightweight agents.
- [Deployment Topologies / HCI (Hyper-Converged)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/deployment-topologies/hci.md): Hyper-converged simplyblock deployments run storage nodes on the same Kubernetes workers as the applications, with optional, best-effort data locality.
- [Deployment Topologies / Disaggregated](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/deployment-topologies/disaggregated.md): Disaggregated simplyblock deployments run storage nodes on dedicated workers of the same Kubernetes cluster, decoupling storage from the compute lifecycle.
- [Deployment Topologies / Edge Clusters](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/deployment-topologies/edge-clusters.md): Small simplyblock storage clusters with one or two nodes at edge sites, managed by a central control plane on a hub cluster.
- [Deployment Topologies / Superclusters](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/deployment-topologies/superclusters.md): Superclusters combine several simplyblock storage clusters into one cluster for Kubernetes, with volumes placed per volume into placement groups.
- [Concepts](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/index.md): The core concepts of simplyblock: clusters, pools, logical volumes, snapshots, erasure coding, failure domains, migration, and disaster recovery.
- [Concepts / Simplyblock Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/simplyblock-cluster.md): A simplyblock deployment consists of a control plane and one or more storage clusters, whose storage nodes take primary, secondary, and tertiary roles.
- [Concepts / Storage Pooling](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/storage-pooling.md): Simplyblock aggregates the devices of all storage nodes into one storage cluster and divides it into storage pools, which carry limits and volume defaults.
- [Concepts / Logical Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/logical-volumes.md): Logical volumes in simplyblock are thin-provisioned virtual NVMe devices, carved from a storage pool and spread across all devices of a storage cluster.
- [Concepts / NVMe Namespaces And Subsystems](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/nvme-namespaces-and-subsystems.md): How simplyblock exposes volumes as NVMe namespaces in NVMe-oF subsystems, and when several volumes should share one subsystem.
- [Concepts / NVMe over Fabrics Security](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/nvmf-security.md): NVMe-oF security in simplyblock provides host access control, DH-HMAC-CHAP authentication, and TLS/PSK encryption for NVMe-oF connections.
- [Concepts / Persistent Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/persistent-volumes.md): How Kubernetes persistent volumes map onto simplyblock logical volumes: provisioning, access modes, reclaim policies, and multipath NVMe-oF connections.
- [Concepts / External Key Management](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/external-key-management.md): How simplyblock encrypts data at rest against an external key management system, and what separation of duty, key rotation, and audit that buys.
- [Concepts / Distributed File Storage](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/distributed-file-storage.md): How simplyblock provides shared file storage: pNFS separates file metadata from file data, so many nodes read and write one filesystem directly over NVMe/TCP.
- [Concepts / ReadWriteMany (pNFS)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/pnfs.md): How simplyblock serves ReadWriteMany volumes through pNFS: a metadata server per storage cluster, direct NVMe-oF data paths, layouts, and restarts.
- [Concepts / Snapshots and Clones](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/snapshots-clones.md): Simplyblock snapshots capture a volume instantly with copy-on-write, and clones turn any snapshot into a writable volume without copying data.
- [Concepts / Snapshot Copy-on-Write](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/snapshot-copy-on-write.md): Simplyblock turns the copy-on-write after a snapshot into a metadata-only page copy and merges the data back when the snapshot is deleted.
- [Concepts / Erasure Coding](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/erasure-coding.md): How simplyblock protects data with distributed erasure coding: data and parity chunks on different nodes, the supported schemes, and their overhead.
- [Concepts / Linux Block Devices (lblk)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/linux-block-devices.md): How simplyblock clusters use arbitrary Linux block devices, such as SAS or SATA SSDs and cloud volumes, instead of NVMe PCIe devices.
- [Concepts / Storage Arrays (FC, iSCSI, NVMe-oF)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/storage-arrays.md): How simplyblock runs on LUNs of an existing FC, iSCSI, or NVMe-oF storage array, and which tasks stay with the array and which move to simplyblock.
- [Concepts / Automatic Rebalancing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/automatic-rebalancing.md): How simplyblock rebalances data across devices and nodes after failures, expansions, and removals, with bounded impact on client I/O.
- [Concepts / Volume Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/volume-migration.md): How simplyblock separates front and back storage, and how the backing logical volume of a volume moves between storage nodes during a migration.
- [Concepts / Failure Domains](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/failure-domains.md): How simplyblock failure domains group storage nodes by rack, cabinet, or availability zone and constrain data, journal, and failover-path placement.
- [Concepts / Placement Groups](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/placement-groups.md): How a simplyblock supercluster places each volume in one placement group, what stays inside a placement group, and how volumes move between them.
- [Concepts / DR Protection Plans](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/dr-protection-plans.md): A protection plan declares the DR sites, the storage classes to protect, the replication methods, and the S3 stores. DR paths declare the allowed directions.
- [Concepts / DR Applications](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/dr-applications.md): A protected application binds workloads and volumes to a protection plan as a discovered or managed application, with tiers, hooks, probes, and path readiness.
- [Concepts / Failover](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/failover.md): Planned relocation with a final sync and no data loss versus unplanned failover with an RPO, readiness gating, overrides, metro fencing, and failback.
- [Concepts / Relocation](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/relocation.md): Restart-based relocation of whole workloads between sites with simplyblock DR, and the online migration of volumes between clusters and nodes.

## Deployment Preparation

- [Deployment Preparation](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/index.md): Plan a simplyblock deployment before installing it: the architecture, fault tolerance, sizing, hardware and storage devices, network, and software.
- [Deployment Architectures](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/deployment-architectures.md): Supported simplyblock architectures with and without disaster recovery: single or multiple storage clusters, a DR hub (metro, async, backup), and a central hub.
- [Fault Tolerance and Erasure Coding](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/erasure-coding-scheme.md): Choose the erasure coding scheme and fault tolerance of a simplyblock cluster: supported schemes, minimum nodes, failure domains, small clusters, and arrays.
- [Sizing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/sizing.md): Size simplyblock storage nodes and the control plane: vCPUs, memory, NUMA placement, hyper-converged shares, and the observability stack.
- [Hardware and Storage Devices](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/hardware-requirements.md): Minimum hardware of simplyblock storage nodes, supported CPU architectures and virtualization, and the requirements for NVMe devices and Linux block devices.
- [Storage Arrays](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/storage-arrays.md): Plan a simplyblock deployment on FC, iSCSI, or NVMe-oF storage array LUNs: LUN layout per host, RAID and erasure coding, thin pools, and multipathing.
- [Network](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/network.md): Network requirements of simplyblock: redundant storage networks, NVMe/TCP and NVMe/RoCE fabrics, management traffic, edge sites, and the ports to open.
- [Software Requirements](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/software-requirements.md): Supported Kubernetes distributions and versions, host operating systems and kernels, NVMe multipathing on client nodes, and the requirements of pNFS.

## Kubernetes Storage

- [Kubernetes Storage](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/index.md): Kubernetes Storage: Simplyblock runs natively on Kubernetes, where it is deployed and managed by the Simplyblock Operator through Custom Resource Definitions.
- [Install](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/index.md): Install simplyblock on Kubernetes: Helm installs the operator, then custom resources drive the control plane, CSI driver, and storage cluster.
- [Install / Control Plane Cluster Architecture](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/management-cluster-architecture.md): The simplyblock control plane on Kubernetes: the ControlPlane resource with its two sources, the installed components, and FoundationDB redundancy.
- [Install / Install Simplyblock Operator](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/k8s-control-plane.md): Install the Simplyblock Operator with Helm. The operator installs the control plane and CSI driver from the ControlPlane and SimplyblockDriver resources.
- [Install / Securing the Control Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/security.md): Configure TLS and mutual TLS for simplyblock control plane traffic on Kubernetes and store volume encryption keys in HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao.
- [Install / Deploying OpenBao as a KMS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/openbao-kms.md): Step-by-step guide that deploys OpenBao on Kubernetes and wires it into a simplyblock cluster as the external key management system for volume encryption.
- [Install / Create a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/k8s-storage-plane.md): Create a simplyblock storage cluster: discover workers and devices, review and approve the ClusterDeploymentConfig, and provision a first volume.
- [Install / Storage Network](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/storage-network.md): Storage network options for simplyblock on Kubernetes: host network, pod network, and Multus with host-device, macvlan, ipvlan, VLAN, and SR-IOV.
- [Install / Cluster Deployment Options](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/cluster-deployment-options.md): The options of a simplyblock storage cluster deployed by the operator: what is set in the deployment document, what is fixed at creation, and what can change.
- [Install / Connecting to an External Control Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/install-csi.md): Use the managed profile of the Simplyblock Operator to consume simplyblock storage from a control plane outside the Kubernetes cluster.
- [Install / Deploying Edge Clusters](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/edge-clusters.md): Deploy a simplyblock edge cluster with one or two nodes: prepare the hub, install the operator in the managed profile, and approve the draft.
- [Install / Air Gap Installation](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/air-gap.md): Air Gap Installation: Simplyblock can be installed in an air-gapped environment.
- [Install / EKS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/eks.md): Prepare and install simplyblock on EKS: instance types, dedicated node groups, taints, node images, EBS storage, Helm values, and discovery.
- [Install / Storage Network on Amazon EKS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/eks-storage-network.md): Attach a dedicated data ENI to simplyblock storage nodes on Amazon EKS with Cilium ENI mode and Multus, in the node subnet or a dedicated subnet.
- [Install / GKE](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/gke.md): Prepare a GKE cluster for simplyblock: recommended machine types with local NVMe SSDs, dedicated node pools, taints, node images, and control plane storage.
- [Install / OpenShift](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/openshift.md): Install simplyblock on OpenShift through OperatorHub: SCC grants, the subscription, the control plane, the storage cluster, and the CSI driver.
- [Install / SUSE Rancher and RKE2](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/rancher.md): Installing simplyblock into RKE2 or K3s clusters managed by SUSE Rancher, including the permissions required on CIS-hardened clusters.
- [Install / Talos](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/talos.md): Run simplyblock on Talos Linux: required kernel modules, huge pages, CPU topology, privileged namespace, and the Talos environment setting.
- [Usage](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/index.md): Use simplyblock volumes on Kubernetes through the simplyblock CSI driver: StorageClasses, provisioning, QoS, encryption, placement, snapshots, clones, and expansion.
- [Usage / Storage Class](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/storage-class.md): How simplyblock StorageClasses are assigned to a StoragePool by labels, how pool volumeDefaults map to class parameters, and which parameters the CSI driver reads.
- [Usage / Provisioning](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/provisioning.md): Provisioning a new PersistentVolume using simplyblock's Kubernetes CSI driver integration requires at least one StorageClass to be set up.
- [Usage / Volume Encryption](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/volume-encryption.md): Encrypt simplyblock logical volumes at rest using the AES_XTS crypto bdev. Keys are managed by the cluster and can optionally be offloaded to an external KMS.
- [Usage / Automatic Volume Placement](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/volume-placement.md): Reference for the PVC annotations and StorageCluster fields that control which storage node becomes a new volume's primary node, and how a pin change migrates a volume.
- [Usage / ReadWriteMany Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/pnfs.md): Provision ReadWriteMany simplyblock volumes on Kubernetes through pNFS: enabling the metadata server, the StorageClass, node requirements, and limitations.
- [Usage / Snapshotting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/snapshotting.md): Snapshot simplyblock PersistentVolumes with VolumeSnapshots, take crash-consistent group snapshots, and restore a whole group with VolumeGroupSnapshotOps.
- [Usage / Cloning](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/cloning.md): Clone a simplyblock-backed PersistentVolumeClaim instantly through a copy-on-write clone, named as the dataSource of a new claim.
- [Usage / Expanding](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/expanding.md): Expand a simplyblock-backed PersistentVolume online by raising the size of its claim, with the filesystem grown in place by the CSI driver.
- [Usage / Removing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/removing.md): Remove simplyblock-backed volumes through the Kubernetes lifecycle, and clean up retained PersistentVolumes and their logical volumes.
- [Usage / Defining Quality of Service](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/quality-of-service.md): Set per-volume IOPS and throughput ceilings for simplyblock volumes through pool volume defaults, StorageClass parameters, or PVC annotations.
- [Usage / Service Classes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/service-classes.md): Define the I/O service classes of a storage cluster, place volumes in a class through a storage pool or StorageClass, and set the share of replication traffic.
- [Operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/index.md): Operate a simplyblock deployment on Kubernetes through the Ops resources of the Simplyblock Operator: lifecycle, data protection, monitoring, and security.
- [Operations / Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/index.md): Operate a simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes: request cluster operations, restart it node by node, upgrade it, and set its data placement.
- [Operations / Cluster / Storage Cluster Actions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/cluster-actions.md): Request cluster-wide lifecycle operations on a simplyblock storage cluster with a StorageClusterOps resource, and track them through their steps.
- [Operations / Cluster / Activating a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/activating-a-cluster.md): Activate a simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes with an Activate operation, and learn when the operator raises the activation on its own.
- [Operations / Cluster / Shutting Down a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/shutting-down-a-cluster.md): Suspend an entire simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes with a Shutdown operation, and learn what it means for the volumes the cluster serves.
- [Operations / Cluster / Starting a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/starting-a-cluster.md): Bring a suspended simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes back into service with a Start operation, and follow the rebalancing that may follow it.
- [Operations / Cluster / Restarting a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/restarting-a-cluster.md): Restart an entire simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes with a Restart operation, which sequences a shutdown and a start, and follow its two steps.
- [Operations / Cluster / Rolling Restart](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/rolling-restart.md): Restart every storage node of a simplyblock cluster in sequence with a RollingRestart operation, optionally replacing the storage-node pod on each worker.
- [Operations / Cluster / Upgrading a Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/cluster-upgrade.md): Upgrade the Simplyblock Operator and its CRDs with Helm, move the control plane with a ControlPlaneOps Upgrade, and roll the storage plane node by node.
- [Operations / Cluster / Upgrading EKS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/eks-upgrade.md): Upgrade the Kubernetes version of an EKS cluster that runs simplyblock: the EKS control plane, the control plane node group, and new storage capacity.
- [Operations / Cluster / Managing Failure Domains](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/failure-domains.md): Enable failure-domain mode on a simplyblock cluster and label Kubernetes workers with fault groups, so erasure-coding chunks are spread across racks or zones.
- [Operations / Cluster / Configuring Node Affinity](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/node-affinity.md): Enable node affinity on a simplyblock cluster so a volume's data stays local to the storage node that owns it, and keep it local with data realignment.
- [Operations / Cluster / Operating Edge Clusters](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/edge-clusters.md): Operation specific to simplyblock edge clusters: monitoring from the hub, failure behavior, maintenance, healing, upgrades, and troubleshooting.
- [Operations / Cluster / Operating on Storage Arrays](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/storage-arrays.md): Operate a simplyblock cluster on storage array LUNs: capacity on two thin-provisioning levels, adding capacity, LUN resizing, failures, and data protection.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/index.md): Operate the storage nodes of a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes: request node operations, move a node to another worker, remove it, or replace it.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Storage Node Actions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/storage-node-actions.md): Request an operation against a single simplyblock storage node with a StorageNodeOps resource, track it through its steps, and restart a single device.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Shutting Down a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/shutting-down-a-storage-node.md): Stop a single simplyblock storage node with a Shutdown operation of a StorageNodeOps resource, and learn the conditions under which it is held or refused.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Restarting a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/restarting-a-storage-node.md): Restart a single simplyblock storage node with a Restart operation of a StorageNodeOps resource, optionally forced and reattaching its volumes.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Suspending a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/suspending-a-storage-node.md): Suspend a single simplyblock storage node with a Suspend operation, so that no new volume is placed on it while it keeps serving the volumes it holds.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Resuming a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/resuming-a-storage-node.md): Return a suspended simplyblock storage node to normal service with a Resume operation of a StorageNodeOps resource, so new volumes are placed on it again.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Replacing a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/replacing-a-storage-node.md): Replace the host under a simplyblock storage node, or retire a node and add a replacement, without making the logical volumes it owns inaccessible.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Migrating a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/migrating-a-storage-node.md): Relocate a simplyblock storage node onto a different Kubernetes worker with a Migrate operation, keeping its backend identity, devices, and logical volumes.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Removing a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/removing-a-storage-node.md): Drain and remove a simplyblock storage node with a Remove operation, which evacuates its volumes onto the remaining nodes before the node leaves the cluster.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Coordinated Worker Node Drain](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/node-drain-coordination.md): How the Simplyblock Operator protects storage availability with a HostMaintenance operation when a Kubernetes worker is cordoned and drained.
- [Operations / Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/index.md): Operate simplyblock volumes on Kubernetes: migrate the backing logical volume, reclaim unused blocks, and recover a workload after a path loss.
- [Operations / Volumes / Volume Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/volume-migration.md): Move the backing logical volume of a PersistentVolume between storage nodes with PersistentVolumeOps, by hand, on a pin change, or when a node is drained.
- [Operations / Volumes / Trimming a Filesystem](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/trimming.md): Reclaim the unused blocks of a thin-provisioned simplyblock volume by trimming its filesystem with fstrim.
- [Operations / Volumes / Recovering from Path Loss](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/path-loss-recovery.md): How the simplyblock CSI node plugin restores NVMe-oF paths after a storage node outage, and how to opt a workload into an automatic pod restart.
- [Operations / Scaling](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/index.md): Scale a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes by adding workers with a growth ClusterDeploymentConfig, and control how many are provisioned at a time.
- [Operations / Scaling / Expanding a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/expanding-storage-cluster.md): Add storage nodes to a running simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes with a growth ClusterDeploymentConfig, and follow the integration of every new node.
- [Operations / Scaling / Parallel Storage Node Addition](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/parallel-node-addition.md): How the Simplyblock Operator adds storage nodes in parallel within a node-provisioning budget, while workers that host FoundationDB are added one at a time.
- [Operations / Scaling / Managing Superclusters](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/superclusters.md): Create, grow, and operate a simplyblock supercluster on Kubernetes: placement groups, storage pools, placement control, and relocating volumes.
- [Operations / Data Protection](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/index.md): Protect the data of a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes with policy-driven backups to S3, asynchronous replication, and FoundationDB backups.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Backup and Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/backup-recovery.md): Policy-driven and on-demand backups of simplyblock volumes to S3-compatible object storage, listed as StorageBackup objects and restored with StorageBackupOps.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Asynchronous Replication](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/asynchronous-replication.md): Configure snapshot-based asynchronous replication between simplyblock clusters with the ReplicationPair, ReplicationPolicy, and ReplicationOps resources.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Online Cluster Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/online-cluster-migration.md): Move volumes online from one simplyblock cluster to another with migration plans: forecast, dry run, one volume per node, and a short-freeze cutover.
- [Operations / Data Protection / FoundationDB Backup and Restore](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/foundationdb-backup.md): Back up and restore the FoundationDB key-value store behind the simplyblock control plane with the FoundationDBBackup and FoundationDBRestore CRDs.
- [Operations / Monitoring](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/index.md): Monitor a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes through the status of its custom resources, the capacity metrics API, Grafana dashboards, alerts, and Graylog.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Cluster Health](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/cluster-health.md): Check the health of a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes through the ControlPlane, StorageCluster, StorageNode, and StorageDevice status, and with the CLI.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Logical Volume Conditions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/lvol-conditions.md): Check the capacity, health, and I/O statistics of the logical volume behind a simplyblock PersistentVolumeClaim with the metrics API, Prometheus, and the CLI.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Device Health](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/device-health.md): Slow-device detection and SMART health checks of the Simplyblock Operator, recorded on each StorageDevice and reported as alerts.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Alerting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/alerts.md): Pre-defined Grafana alert rules of the simplyblock control plane on Kubernetes, their notification channels configured through Helm, and the alerts endpoint.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Prometheus Metrics](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/prometheus-metrics.md): Reference of the simplyblock Prometheus metrics: I/O, latency, capacity, status, CPU, and replication series of the control plane, and the operator metrics.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Accessing Grafana](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/accessing-grafana.md): Enable the Grafana dashboards of a simplyblock control plane on Kubernetes, reach them through a port-forward, and retrieve the admin password.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Accessing Graylog](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/accessing-graylog.md): Reach the Graylog log search of a simplyblock control plane on Kubernetes through a port-forward and retrieve its admin password.
- [Operations / Security](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/security/index.md): Secure a simplyblock deployment on Kubernetes: authenticate the NVMe-oF transport per storage pool, encrypt volumes, and isolate tenants from each other.
- [Operations / Security / Host Authentication and Encryption](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/security/authentication-encryption.md): Host access control and DH-HMAC-CHAP authentication for NVMe-oF on Kubernetes, configured on a StoragePool and its StorageClass.
- [Operations / Security / Multi-Tenancy](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/security/multi-tenancy.md): Isolate tenants on Kubernetes with one StorageCluster per namespace, StoragePools as tenancy units, and the RBAC aggregate roles.

## Disaster Recovery

- [Disaster Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/index.md): simplyblock Disaster Recovery protects Kubernetes applications and KubeVirt VMs on simplyblock across sites with failover, relocation, tests, and backups.
- [Install](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/install/index.md): Installation flow of simplyblock Disaster Recovery: the hub cluster, the archive, the state bundle, the site clusters, and the components each of them runs.
- [Install / Disaster Recovery Requirements](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/install/requirements.md): Requirements for simplyblock Disaster Recovery: hub cluster sizing, Kubernetes versions, site cluster prerequisites, S3 buckets, networking, and site labeling.
- [Install / Installing the Hub](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/install/hub.md): Install the dr-simplyblock-hub Helm chart, which bootstraps OCM and Ramen, deploys dr-hub, and creates the DR roles on the hub cluster.
- [Install / Archive and State Bundle](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/install/archive.md): Configure the S3 archive for DR reports, the signing key, and the signed DR state bundle that is used to rebuild a lost hub cluster.
- [Install / Joining Site Clusters](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/install/sites.md): Join site clusters to the DR hub with a bootstrap token and the dr-simplyblock-spoke chart, and verify the site stack the hub delivers.
- [Configuration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/index.md): The configuration model of simplyblock Disaster Recovery: DR configuration, protection plans, DR paths, protected applications, tiers, hooks, and Recipes.
- [Configuration / Replication Types](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/replication-types.md): The five replication method types of simplyblock Disaster Recovery: sync, async, s3-backup, and their combinations, with use cases, recovery points, prerequisites, and constraints.
- [Configuration / Protection Plans](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/protection-plans.md): Declare sites, protected StorageClasses, replication methods, and S3 stores with a ProtectionPlan, and monitor its readiness and conditions.
- [Configuration / DR Paths](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/paths.md): Declare the directions between the sites of a protection plan with DRPath resources, the actions allowed along each direction, and the test environment.
- [Configuration / Protected Applications](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/applications.md): Protect discovered and GitOps-managed applications with a ProtectedApplication: namespaces, PVC selection, source, target, method, and probes.
- [Configuration / Workflows and Recipes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/workflows-and-recipes.md): Define the boot order of an application on the target site with tiers and ready conditions, add external hooks, and use hand-written Ramen Recipes.
- [Configuration / Site Profiles and Mappings](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/site-profiles.md): Describe each site with a SiteProfile, bind network roles and DHCP servers, and let the site mapper rewrite VM network attachments and reserve guest addresses on the target.
- [Configuration / Access Control](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/configuration/access-control.md): The dr-viewer, dr-operator, and dr-admin roles, the override verb for readiness overrides, creator stamping, and the admission checks.
- [Discovery and Proposals](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/discovery/index.md): Simplyblock DR discovers applications, their dependencies, and their site mappings, and proposes the complete protection setup of each for approval.
- [Discovery and Proposals / Setup](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/discovery/setup.md): Enable discovery in the DR configuration, run the eBPF flow collector on the sites, connect a GitOps repository, and grant the roles for approval.
- [Discovery and Proposals / Using Discovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/discovery/using-discovery.md): Run discovery, read the graph and candidates of a site, review a bundle, approve it through a pull request or in the Control Center, and roll it back.
- [Discovery and Proposals / Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/discovery/reference.md): Reference of discovery: graphs, bundles with their phases, DR configuration settings, discovery runs, request annotations, and the allowed label keys.
- [Discovery and Proposals / Environment Promotion](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/discovery/blueprints.md): Export the approved DR setup of a test environment as a blueprint and propose it in production, matched against the production site, for approval.
- [Discovery and Proposals / Migration From VMware Live Site Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/discovery/srm-import.md): Import the protection groups and recovery plans of VMware Live Site Recovery (SRM) and propose them for the VMs migrated to KubeVirt, for approval.
- [Test](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/testing/index.md): Why and how to rehearse a disaster recovery failover with simplyblock DR test bubbles, what a test proves, and how recent tests affect readiness.
- [Test / Test Failover](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/testing/test-failover.md): Run a test failover with a TestBubble: clone replicated volumes on the target site, restore in isolation, validate, report, and tear down.
- [Test / Test Schedules](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/testing/test-schedules.md): Run simplyblock DR test failovers automatically on a cron schedule with a TestSchedule. Covers retention, suspension, overlap, and missed runs.
- [Operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/index.md): Operating simplyblock DR with recovery actions: monitoring, failover, relocation, recovery plans, backups, restores, and recovery of a lost hub.
- [Operations / Monitoring](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/monitoring.md): Monitor simplyblock DR: readiness verdicts and checks, status fields, kubectl views, events, Prometheus metrics, suggested alerts, and the report archive.
- [Operations / Planned Failover](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/planned-failover.md): Move an application to its DR site without data loss with a Relocate recovery action: pre-checks, final sync, phases, rollback, hooks, and the report.
- [Operations / Unplanned Failover](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/unplanned-failover.md): Recover an application on the DR site after the loss of its primary site with a Failover recovery action, including overrides, achieved RPO, and cleanup.
- [Operations / Relocate (Restart)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/relocate-restart.md): Move workloads between sites by restart with simplyblock DR: failback after a failover, permanent moves, application impact, and cleanup on the source.
- [Operations / Relocate (Online)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/relocate-online.md): Online relocation of running workloads between sites without restart: cross-cluster VM live migration (coming soon) and online volume migration.
- [Operations / Restart After a Storage Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/restart.md): Restart protected applications in place and in boot order after their storage cluster recovers from a suspension, automatically per plan or with a Restart action.
- [Operations / Recovery Plans](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/recovery-plans.md): Fail over or relocate several applications in order with a RecoveryPlan: priorities, dependencies, gates, failure handling, and plan-level hooks.
- [Operations / Backup and Restore](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/backup-restore.md): Back up protected applications to S3 with the backup method types and restore them onto rebuilt sites with a RestoreAction after the loss of the hub and every site.
- [Operations / Hub Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/operations/hub-recovery.md): Recover a lost simplyblock DR hub cluster from its signed state bundle with dr-restore, re-join the sites, and fail over when the primary site is lost too.
- [Control Center](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/disaster-recovery/control-center.md): Deploy the simplyblock Control Center with the operator or the DR hub chart and manage plans, paths, applications, site mappings, actions, and tests in the browser.

## Command Assistant

- [Command Assistant](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/assistant/index.md): Describe a task, such as installing simplyblock on a three-node OpenShift cluster, and get the documented commands in the order to run them.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/tutorials/index.md): Short explainer videos on simplyblock: core storage, file and object storage, disaster recovery (DR), and edge clusters.

## Reference

- [Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/index.md): Reference: Simplyblock provides multiple interfaces for managing and interacting with its distributed storage system, including the command-line interface (CLI).
- [API / Developer SDK](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/api/index.md): API / Developer SDK: Simplyblock offers a comprehensive API to manage and automate cluster operations.
- [API / Developer SDK / Alerts Endpoint](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/api/alerts.md): REST endpoint returning the conditions in a simplyblock cluster that currently need an operator, suppressing operator-initiated states, with Slack integration.
- [API / Developer SDK / API Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/api/reference.md): Interactive Simplyblock API reference generated from OpenAPI, with endpoint details, request/response schemas, and integration-oriented examples.
- [CLI / Command-line interface](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/index.md): CLI / Command-line interface: Simplyblock provides a feature-rich CLI (command line interface) client to manage all aspects of the storage cluster.
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Storage Node Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/storage-node.md): Aliases: sn
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Cluster Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/cluster.md): Cluster Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Logical Volume Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/volume.md): Aliases: lvol
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Control Plane Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/control-plane.md): Aliases: cp mgmt
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Storage Pool Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/storage-pool.md): Aliases: pool
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Snapshot Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/snapshot.md): Snapshot Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Consistency Group Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/consistency-group.md): Aliases: cg
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Backup Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/backup.md): Backup Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Consistency-group backup commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/group-backup.md): Aliases: gb
- [CLI / Command-line interface / QoS Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/qos.md): QoS Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / FDB Backup operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/db-backup.md): FDB Backup operations
- [Simplyblock Operator](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/operator/index.md): Overview of the Simplyblock Operator API storage.simplyblock.io/v1alpha2: served versions, resource kinds, the common Ops shape, metrics, and label keys.
- [Simplyblock Operator / Simplyblock Operator Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/operator/reference.md): Reference for Simplyblock Operator Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs).
- [Simplyblock Helm Chart](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/kubernetes/index.md): Overview of the simplyblock-operator Helm chart: what it renders per deployment profile, and example values files for the common deployment scenarios.
- [Simplyblock Helm Chart / Simplyblock Helm Chart Values](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/kubernetes/helm-values.md): Generated reference of every value of the simplyblock-operator Helm chart, with its type and default, grouped by top-level key.
- [Limits](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/limits.md): Hard object limits and vCPU-dependent resource limits of simplyblock storage nodes and clusters: subsystems, namespaces, objects per node, and sizing rules.
- [Upgrade Matrix](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/upgrade-matrix.md): Upgrade Matrix: Simplyblock supports in-place upgrades of existing clusters. However, not all versions can be upgraded straight to the latest versions.
- [Supported Linux Distributions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/supported-linux-distributions.md): Supported Linux Distributions: Simplyblock requires a Linux Kernel 5.19 or later with NVMe over Fabrics and NVMe over TCP enabled.
- [Supported Linux Kernels](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/supported-linux-kernels.md): Supported Linux Kernels: Simplyblock is built upon NVMe over Fabrics. Hence, it requires a Linux kernel with NVMe and NVMe-oF support.
- [NVMe Low-Level Format](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/nvme-low-level-format.md): Guide to NVMe low-level formatting for Simplyblock environments, including when formatting is needed and how to prepare devices safely.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/index.md): Troubleshooting: Simplyblock is designed as a system for minimal manual intervention.
- [Troubleshooting / Control Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/control-plane.md): Control Plane: Symptom: FoundationDB error. All services that rely upon the FoundationDB key-value storage are offline or refuse to start.
- [Troubleshooting / Storage Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/storage-plane.md): Storage Plane: Symptom: After a fresh deployment, the cluster cannot be activated.
- [Troubleshooting / Kubernetes CSI](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/simplyblock-csi.md): Kubernetes CSI: Controller Plugin runs as a StatefulSet and manages volume provisioning and deletion. Node Plugin runs as a DaemonSet and handles volume attachment and mounts.
